title: The meeting is in progress
goal: Read and write the formal progressive -mAktA(dIr) of news, notices and announcements.

intro.text: News and notices use `-mAktA` instead of `-(I)yor`, with the endings of **to be** and, in the third person, `-DIr`: *Toplantı devam etmektedir* (The meeting is in progress), *Konu incelenmektedir* (The matter is being examined). In conversation, keep `-(I)yor`.

vocab.en: to continue, to last; to drive
official, person in charge; the authorities (yetkililer)
intense, heavy; busy (yoğun bakım: intensive care)
valuable; dear, esteemed (Değerli yolcularımız: dear passengers)

exercises.question: *Yetkililer konuyu incelemektedir.* What does it mean?
options: The authorities are examining the matter.
The authorities must examine the matter.
exercises.explain: `-mAktAdIr` is the formal present progressive: *incele-mekte-dir* means the same as *inceliyor*.

exercises.en: The roadworks are still going on.
exercises.explain: Still going on now: the present, positive, *devam et-mekte-dir*. *Etmekteydi* is the past, *etmemektedir* the negative.

exercises.label: *çalışmak*, formal progressive: I am working, you are working…
exercises.explain: The endings of **to be** after a buffer y: *çalış-makta-y-ım*. The third person usually adds `-DIr`: *çalışmaktadır*, *çalışmaktadırlar*.

accept: The patient is being treated in intensive care.
The patient is [receiving treatment|under treatment] in intensive care.
The patient is being treated in [the intensive care unit|the ICU].
The patient is currently [being treated|receiving treatment] in [intensive care|the intensive care unit].

exercises.prompt: Prices are rising. (formal, as in the news)

reject.why: Right in conversation. The news would say *artmaktadır*, with `-mAktA` and `-DIr`.

exercises.explain: *art-makta-dır*: the formal progressive, with `-DIr` in the third person.

exercises.en: The cause of the accident is being investigated.

exercises.text: The matter is being examined by the authorities.
accept: The matter is being examined by the officials.

exercises.question: Which would you say to a friend on the phone?

why.1: `-mAktA` belongs to news and notices; to a friend it sounds like a press release.
why.2: Neither the formal `-DIr` nor `-mAktA` belongs in a phone call with a friend.

exercises.prompt: At that time the museum was being restored. (formal)

reject.why: *Onarılmaktadır* is the present. For **was being**, add `-(y)DI`: *onarılmaktaydı*.
Right in conversation; in a formal text, use *onarılmaktaydı*.

exercises.explain: Passive *-ıl*, formal progressive *-makta*, then `-DIr`, all with back vowels: *yap-ıl-makta-dır*.

exercises.prompt: Değerli yolcularımız, trenimiz on dakika gecikmeli olarak gelmektedir.
accept: Dear passengers, our train is arriving ten minutes late.
Dear passengers, our train is arriving 10 minutes late.
Dear passengers, our train is [coming|running] [ten|10] minutes late.
Dear passengers, our train is arriving with a [ten|10] minute delay.
Dear passengers, our train is delayed by [ten|10] minutes.

exercises.task: Rewrite this note as a formal notice for the entrance of your building. Use `-mAktAdIr` and the passive, and a polite request.
exercises.source: Asansörü tamir ediyorlar. Bu hafta merdivenleri kullanın, lütfen.
models: Asansör tamir edilmektedir. Bu hafta boyunca lütfen merdivenleri kullanınız.
Değerli komşularımız, asansörümüzde onarım çalışması yapılmaktadır. Çalışma bu hafta sürecektir; bu süre içinde merdivenleri kullanmanızı rica ederiz.
checklist: The passive hides who does the work: *tamir edilmektedir*
The request is polite: *kullanınız*, or *kullanmanızı rica ederiz*
